metadata.title: On Ideal Lattices and Learning with Errors Over Rings
metadata.authors: Vadim Lyubashevsky, Chris Peikert, Oded Regev
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Smoothing parameter
nodes.statement: For a lattice $\Lambda$ and positive real $\varepsilon > 0$, the smoothing parameter $\eta_\varepsilon(\Lambda)$ is the smallest $r$ such that $\rho_{1/r}(\Lambda^* \setminus \{0\}) \leq \varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_clean: Smallest Gaussian width that makes the dual lattice look uniform modulo the lattice.

nodes.name: K-SVP and K-SIVP on ideal lattices
nodes.statement: Given a fractional ideal $I$ in $K$ and $\gamma \geq 1$: $K$-$\mathrm{SVP}_\gamma$ asks for nonzero $x \in I$ with $\|x\| \leq \gamma \cdot \lambda_1(I)$; $K$-$\mathrm{SIVP}_\gamma$ asks for $n$ linearly independent elements of $I$ with norms at most $\gamma \cdot \lambda_n(I)$.

nodes.name: K-BDD on ideal lattices
nodes.statement: Given a fractional ideal $I$ in $K$ and $d < \lambda_1(I)/2$: $K$-$\mathrm{BDD}_{I,d}$ asks, given $y = x + e$ for $x \in I$ and $\|e\| \leq d$, to recover $x$.

nodes.name: Ring-LWE distribution $A_{s,\psi}$
nodes.statement: For $s \in R_q^\vee$ and error distribution $\psi$ over $K_\mathbb{R}$, a sample is $(a, b = (a \cdot s)/q + e \bmod R^\vee)$ where $a \leftarrow R_q$ uniform and $e \leftarrow \psi$.
nodes.statement_clean: The ring-LWE sample is a uniform $a$ paired with a noisy product $a \cdot s/q + e$ in the codifferent torus.

nodes.name: Search Ring-LWE ($R$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi}$)
nodes.statement: Given access to arbitrarily many samples from $A_{s,\psi}$ for arbitrary $s \in R_q^\vee$ and $\psi \in \Psi$, find $s$.

nodes.name: Average-case decision Ring-LWE ($R$-$\mathrm{DLWE}_{q,\Upsilon}$)
nodes.statement: Distinguish samples from $A_{s,\psi}$, for $(s,\psi) \leftarrow U(R_q^\vee) \times \Upsilon$, from uniformly random samples in $R_q \times \mathbb{T}$ with non-negligible advantage.

nodes.name: Error family $\Psi_{\leq \alpha}$
nodes.statement: $\Psi_{\leq \alpha}$ is the set of all elliptical Gaussian distributions $D_r$ over $K_\mathbb{R}$ whose parameters satisfy $r_i \leq \alpha$.

nodes.name: Noise distribution $\Upsilon_\alpha$
nodes.statement: Sampling $\Upsilon_\alpha$ yields an elliptical Gaussian $D_r$ with $r_i^2 = r_{i+n/2}^2 = \alpha^2(1 + \sqrt{n}\, x_i)$ where $x_1,\dots,x_{n/2} \sim \Gamma(2,1)$ independently.

nodes.name: $q$-$\mathrm{BDD}_{I,d}$
nodes.statement: Given a $\mathrm{BDD}_{I,d}$ instance with solution $x \in I$, find $x \bmod qI$.

nodes.name: $\mathfrak{q}_i$-LWE
nodes.statement: Given access to $A_{s,\psi}$ for arbitrary $s \in R_q^\vee$ and $\psi \in \Psi$, find $s \bmod \mathfrak{q}_i R^\vee$.

nodes.name: Hybrid LWE distribution $A^i_{s,\psi}$
nodes.statement: For $i \in \mathbb{Z}_m^*$, $A^i_{s,\psi}$ outputs $(a, b + h/q)$ where $(a,b) \leftarrow A_{s,\psi}$ and $h \in R_q^\vee$ is uniform mod $\mathfrak{q}_j R^\vee$ for $j \leq i$ and $0$ mod the remaining $\mathfrak{q}_j R^\vee$. $A^0_{s,\psi} = A_{s,\psi}$.

nodes.name: Worst-case decision LWE relative to $\mathfrak{q}_i$ (WDLWE$^i$)
nodes.statement: Given access to $A^j_{s,\psi}$ for arbitrary $s \in R_q^\vee$, $\psi \in \Psi$, and $j \in \{i-, i\}$, find $j$.

nodes.name: Average-case decision LWE relative to $\mathfrak{q}_i$ (DLWE$^i_{q,\Upsilon}$)
nodes.statement: An algorithm solves $\mathrm{DLWE}^i_{q,\Upsilon}$ if, with non-negligible probability over $(s,\psi) \leftarrow U(R_q^\vee) \times \Upsilon$, it has non-negligible difference in acceptance probability on inputs from $A^i_{s,\psi}$ versus $A^{i-}_{s,\psi}$.

nodes.name: Discrete Gaussian Sampling (K-DGS)
nodes.statement: $K$-$\mathrm{DGS}_\gamma$: given an ideal $I$ in $K$ and a number $s \geq \gamma(I)$, produce samples from the discrete Gaussian distribution $D_{I,s}$.

nodes.name: Smoothing parameter bounds
nodes.statement: For any $n$-dimensional lattice $\Lambda$, $\eta_{2^{-2n}}(\Lambda) \leq \sqrt{n}/\lambda_1(\Lambda^*)$, and $\eta_\varepsilon(\Lambda) \leq \sqrt{\ln(n/\varepsilon)} \cdot \lambda_n(\Lambda)$ for all $0 < \varepsilon < 1$.

nodes.name: Smoothing implies near-uniformity
nodes.statement: For any lattice $\Lambda$, $\varepsilon > 0$, $r \geq \eta_\varepsilon(\Lambda)$, and $c \in H$, the statistical distance between $(D_r + c) \bmod \Lambda$ and the uniform distribution mod $\Lambda$ is at most $\varepsilon/2$. Equivalently $\rho_r(\Lambda + c) \in [\frac{1-\varepsilon}{1+\varepsilon}, 1] \cdot \rho_r(\Lambda)$.

nodes.name: Discrete Gaussian tail bound
nodes.statement: For any $n$-dimensional lattice $\Lambda$ and $r > 0$, a point sampled from $D_{\Lambda,r}$ has Euclidean norm at most $r\sqrt{n}$ except with probability at most $2^{-2n}$.

nodes.name: Continuous-noise smoothing
nodes.statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a lattice, $u \in H$, $r,s > 0$, and assume $1/\sqrt{1/r^2 + 1/s^2} \geq \eta_\varepsilon(\Lambda)$ for some $\varepsilon < 1/2$. Sampling from $D_{\Lambda+u,r}$ and adding $D_s$ yields a distribution within statistical distance $4\varepsilon$ of $D_{\sqrt{r^2+s^2}}$.

nodes.name: Ideal-lattice minimum-distance bounds
nodes.statement: For any fractional ideal $I$ in a number field $K$ of degree $n$ and any $\ell_p$ norm with $p \in [1,\infty]$: $n^{1/p} \cdot N(I)^{1/n} \leq \lambda_1(I) \leq n^{1/p} \cdot N(I)^{1/n} \cdot \sqrt{\Delta_K^{1/n}}$.

nodes.name: Chinese Remainder Theorem for $\mathcal{O}_K$
nodes.statement: Let $I_1,\dots,I_r$ be pairwise coprime ideals in $R = \mathcal{O}_K$ and $I = \prod_i I_i$. The natural map $R \to \bigoplus_i (R/I_i)$ induces a ring isomorphism $R/I \to \bigoplus_i (R/I_i)$.

nodes.name: CRT-basis algorithm
nodes.statement: There is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given pairwise coprime ideals $I_1,\dots,I_r$ (as $\mathbb{Z}$-bases), outputs a CRT basis $c_1,\dots,c_r \in R$ with $c_i = 1 \bmod I_i$ and $c_i = 0 \bmod I_j$ for $j \neq i$.

nodes.name: Existence of clearing element
nodes.statement: Let $I, J$ be ideals in $R$. There exists $t \in I$ such that $t \cdot I^{-1} \subseteq R$ is coprime to $J$, and $t$ can be found efficiently given $I$ and the prime factorization of $J$.

nodes.name: Clearing-the-ideal isomorphism
nodes.statement: Let $I, J, M$ be ideals/fractional ideals with $t \in I$ such that $t I^{-1}$ is coprime to $J$. Then $\theta_t(u) = t \cdot u$ induces an $R$-module isomorphism $M / J M \to I M / I J M$, efficiently invertible.

nodes.name: Automorphisms act transitively on $\mathfrak{q}_i$
nodes.statement: Using the splitting $\langle q \rangle = \prod_i \mathfrak{q}_i$ for $q \equiv 1 \bmod m$: for any $i,j \in \mathbb{Z}_m^*$, $\tau_j(\mathfrak{q}_i) = \mathfrak{q}_{i/j}$.

nodes.name: Iterative quantum step
nodes.statement: There exists an efficient quantum algorithm that, given a fractional ideal $I$, $r \geq \sqrt{2} q \cdot \eta_\varepsilon(I)$ with $r' := r \omega(\sqrt{\log n})/(\alpha q) > \sqrt{2n}/\lambda_1(I^\vee)$, an $R$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ oracle, and samples from $D_{I,r}$, outputs a sample from $D_{I,r'}$.

nodes.name: BDD-to-LWE reduction
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha > 0$, $q \geq 2$ with known factorization, $I$ a fractional ideal, and $r \geq \sqrt{2} q \cdot \eta_\varepsilon(I)$. Given a $D_{I,r}$ oracle, there is a probabilistic polynomial-time classical reduction from $\mathrm{BDD}_{I^\vee,d}$ in $\ell_\infty$ to $R$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$, where $d = \alpha q/(\sqrt{2} r)$.

nodes.name: Quantum BDD-to-DGS step (Regev)
nodes.statement: There is an efficient quantum algorithm that, given an $n$-dimensional lattice $\Lambda$, $d' < \lambda_1(\Lambda^\vee)/2$, and a BDD oracle on $\Lambda^\vee$ (succeeding except with negligible probability on Gaussian-offset points), outputs a sample from $D_{\Lambda, \sqrt{n}/(\sqrt{2}d')}$.

nodes.name: BDD reduces to $q$-BDD
nodes.statement: For any $q \geq 2$, there is a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from $\mathrm{BDD}_{I,d}$ to $q$-$\mathrm{BDD}_{I,d}$ in any $\ell_p$ norm.

nodes.name: Correctness of the BDD-to-LWE samples
nodes.statement: Each pair $(a,b)$ produced by the reduction in Section 4.2 from a $\mathrm{BDD}_{I^\vee, d}$ instance $y = x + e$ has distribution $A_{s,\psi}$ (up to negligible statistical distance) for $s = \theta_t(x \bmod qI^\vee) = t \cdot x \in R_q^\vee$ and some $\psi \in \Psi_{\leq \alpha}$.

nodes.name: Multiplicative Gaussian smoothing
nodes.statement: Let $I$ be a fractional ideal in $K$, $r \geq \sqrt{2} \cdot \eta_\varepsilon(I)$, $e \in K$ fixed, $z \sim D_{I+v, r}$ for arbitrary $v$, and $e' \sim D_{r_0}$ with $r_0 \geq r \|e\|_\infty$. Then $z \cdot e + e'$ is within negligible statistical distance of the elliptical Gaussian $D_r'$ with $r'^2_i = r^2 |\sigma_i(e)|^2 + r_0^2$.

nodes.name: LWE to $\mathfrak{q}_i$-LWE via automorphisms
nodes.statement: If the family $\Psi$ is closed under all automorphisms of $K$, then for every $i \in \mathbb{Z}_m^*$ there is a deterministic polynomial-time reduction from $\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi}$ to $\mathfrak{q}_i$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi}$.

nodes.name: $\Psi_{\leq \alpha}$ closed under automorphisms
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha > 0$, $\Psi_{\leq \alpha}$ is closed under every automorphism $\tau$ of $K$: $\psi \in \Psi_{\leq \alpha} \Rightarrow \tau(\psi) \in \Psi_{\leq \alpha}$.

nodes.name: Search-to-decision reduction
nodes.statement: For any $i \in \mathbb{Z}_m^*$, there is a probabilistic polynomial-time reduction from $\mathfrak{q}_i$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi}$ to $\mathrm{WDLWE}^i_{q,\Psi}$.

nodes.name: Worst-case to average-case (non-spherical)
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha > 0$ and every $i \in \mathbb{Z}_m^*$, there is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from $\mathrm{WDLWE}^i_{q, \Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ to $\mathrm{DLWE}^i_{q, \Upsilon_\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Last-hybrid uniformity
nodes.statement: Let $\alpha \geq \eta_\varepsilon(R^\vee)/q$. Then for any $\psi$ in the support of $\Upsilon_\alpha$ and any $s \in R_q^\vee$, the distribution $A^{m-1}_{s,\psi}$ is within statistical distance $\varepsilon/2$ of uniform over $R_q \times \mathbb{T}$.

nodes.name: Hybrid lemma (DLWE to DLWE$^i$)
nodes.statement: If $\Upsilon$ is such that $A^{m-1}_{s,\psi}$ is negligibly far from uniform for any $\psi$ in its support and any $s$, then any oracle solving $\mathrm{DLWE}_{q,\Upsilon}$ yields, for some $i \in \mathbb{Z}_m^*$, an efficient algorithm for $\mathrm{DLWE}^i_{q,\Upsilon}$.

nodes.name: Worst-case to average-case with spherical noise
nodes.statement: For any $\alpha > 0$, $\ell \geq 1$, and every $i \in \mathbb{Z}_m^*$, there is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from $\mathrm{WDLWE}^i_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ to $\mathrm{DLWE}^i_{q, D_\xi}$ given only $\ell$ samples, where $\xi = \alpha (n\ell/\log(n\ell))^{1/4}$.

nodes.name: Main Theorem (Ring-LWE hardness)
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be the $m$th cyclotomic field with $n = \varphi(m)$, $R = \mathcal{O}_K$, $\alpha < \sqrt{\log n / n}$, and $q \equiv 1 \bmod m$ a poly-bounded prime with $\alpha q \geq \omega(\sqrt{\log n})$. Then there is a polynomial-time quantum reduction from $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n}/\alpha)$-approximate SIVP (or SVP) on ideal lattices in $K$ to $R$-$\mathrm{DLWE}_{q,\Upsilon_\alpha}$.
conclusions: Polynomial-time quantum reduction $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{n}/\alpha)$-SIVP/SVP on ideal lattices $\to$ $R$-$\mathrm{DLWE}_{q,\Upsilon_\alpha}$

nodes.name: Hardness of search Ring-LWE
nodes.statement: Let $K$ be a number field of degree $n$, $R = \mathcal{O}_K$, $\alpha = \alpha(n) > 0$, $q = q(n) \geq 2$ with $\alpha q \geq 2 \omega(\sqrt{\log n})$. There is a probabilistic polynomial-time quantum reduction from $K$-$\mathrm{DGS}_\gamma$ to $R$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q, \Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$, with $\gamma = \max\{\eta_\varepsilon(I) \cdot (\sqrt{2}/\alpha) \cdot \omega(\sqrt{\log n}),\, \sqrt{2n}/\lambda_1(I^\vee)\}$.

nodes.name: Search-to-decision (random non-spherical noise)
nodes.statement: Let $R, q$ as in Section 5 and $\alpha q \geq \eta_\varepsilon(R^\vee)$ for some negligible $\varepsilon$. Then there is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from $R$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ to $R$-$\mathrm{DLWE}_{q,\Upsilon_\alpha}$.
assumptions: $R$ ring of integers of cyclotomic field, $q \equiv 1 \bmod m$

nodes.name: Search-to-decision (bounded samples, spherical noise)
nodes.statement: Let $R, q, \alpha$ as in Theorem 5.1, and $\ell \geq 1$. There is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from $R$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ to $R$-$\mathrm{DLWE}_{q,D_\xi}$ given only $\ell$ samples, where $\xi = \alpha \cdot (n\ell/\log(n\ell))^{1/4}$.

nodes.name: Search-to-decision under spherical-search assumption
nodes.statement: Let $R, q, \alpha$ as in Theorem 5.1. There is a randomized polynomial-time reduction from $R$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,D_\alpha}$ to $R$-$\mathrm{DLWE}_{q,D_\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Rényi-divergence transfer for shifted Gamma
nodes.statement: Let $P = \Gamma(2,1)^n$ and $Q = (\Gamma(2,1)-z_1) \times \cdots \times (\Gamma(2,1)-z_n)$ for $0 \leq z_i \leq 1/\sqrt{n}$. Any $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ with non-negligible measure under $P$ also has non-negligible measure under $Q$.

nodes.name: Rényi-divergence transfer for nearby Gaussians
nodes.statement: If $|s_i/r_i - 1| < \sqrt{\log n / n}$ for all $i$, then any $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ with non-negligible measure under $D_{r_1} \times \cdots \times D_{r_n}$ also has non-negligible measure under $D_{s_1} \times \cdots \times D_{s_n}$.

nodes.name: BDD-to-LWE reduction
nodes.statement: Classical reduction transforming a $q$-$\mathrm{BDD}_{I^\vee,d}$ instance $y = x+e$ into ring-LWE samples $A_{s,\psi}$ with $s = t \cdot x$, then inverting the $\theta_t$ map to recover $x \bmod qI^\vee$.

nodes.name: Iterative quantum dimension-reduction (Regev-style)
nodes.statement: Repeatedly apply Lemma 4.2 starting from very wide discrete Gaussian samples $D_{I,r}$ to produce samples $D_{I, r'}$ with progressively narrower parameters until reaching the target $\gamma$.
output: Discrete Gaussian samples $D_{I,\gamma}$ for the target $\gamma$ in Eq. (4.1)

nodes.name: Public-key cryptosystem from Ring-LWE
nodes.statement: Semantically secure PKE: secret $s$, public key $(a, b = a \cdot s + e)$ with small $s, e$; encrypt $z \in \{0,1\}^n$ via $(u, v) = (ar+e_1,\, br + e_2 + \lfloor q/2 \rceil z)$; decrypt by $v - u \cdot s$ and rounding.
output: Ciphertext $(u, v) \in R_q^2$; decryption recovers $z$ via rounding of $v - u s$

nodes.name: Generalized extended Euclidean for CRT basis
nodes.statement: Given Z-bases for coprime ideals $I, J$, compute the HNF basis of $I+J = R$, express $1 \in R$ as a combination $1 = x + y$ with $x \in I$, $y \in J$, and output $c = y$. Iterate to obtain a CRT basis for any pairwise coprime $I_1,\dots,I_r$.
input: Pairwise coprime ideals $I_1, \dots, I_r$ given by $\mathbb{Z}$-bases
output: CRT basis $c_1, \dots, c_r \in R$ with $c_i \equiv 1 \bmod I_i$, $c_i \equiv 0 \bmod I_j$ for $j \neq i$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2 (iterative quantum step)
nodes.statement: Combine Lemma 4.3 (BDD-to-LWE with samples from $D_{I,r}$) and Lemma 4.4 (quantum BDD-to-DGS) with $d_0 = d\sqrt{n}/\omega(\sqrt{\log n})$ to produce samples from $D_{I, r'}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.7
nodes.statement: Show $a$ is near uniform via smoothing (Lemma 2.3) and bijection $\theta_t$ (Lemma 2.15), then expand $b = (z\cdot x)/q + (z/q)\cdot e + e'$ and apply Lemma 4.8 to identify the noise as elliptical Gaussian $D_r$ with $r_i \leq \alpha$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.8
nodes.statement: Write $z\cdot e + e' = (z + e'/e)\cdot e$, decompose $e'/e = f + g$ with $f \sim D_r$, apply Lemma 2.5 to combine $z + f$ into $D_{\sqrt{2}r}$, and conclude.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.5
nodes.statement: Apply automorphism $\tau_k$ with $k = j/i$ to the LWE samples, invoke the $\mathfrak{q}_i$-LWE oracle on $A_{\tau_k(s),\psi'}$, recover $\tau_k(s) \bmod \mathfrak{q}_i R^\vee$, then $\tau_k^{-1}$ to obtain $s \bmod \mathfrak{q}_j R^\vee$ for every $j$, and reconstruct $s$ via CRT.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.9
nodes.statement: For each guess $g$ of $s \bmod \mathfrak{q}_i R^\vee$, transform $(a,b)$ to $(a+v, b+(h+vg)/q)$ with random $v$ (uniform mod $\mathfrak{q}_i$, zero elsewhere) and random $h$. The transformed distribution is $A^{i-}_{s,\psi}$ when $g = s \bmod \mathfrak{q}_i R^\vee$ and $A^i_{s,\psi}$ otherwise; the $\mathrm{WDLWE}^i$ oracle distinguishes.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.12
nodes.statement: Choose random $s' \in R_q^\vee$ and $r'$ from $\Upsilon_\alpha$-style parameters, transform input by adding $(a s' + h)/q + e'$, and use Claim 5.11 (Rényi divergence between $\Gamma(2,1)^n$ and shifted product) to transfer the non-negligible advantage to $\mathrm{DLWE}^i_{q,\Upsilon_\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5.16
nodes.statement: Analogous to the proof of Lemma 5.12 but using Claim 5.15 (Rényi divergence between nearby Gaussians) to transfer non-negligibility from $D_{r_0}^\ell$ to $D_\xi^\ell$ with $\xi = \alpha(n\ell/\log(n\ell))^{1/4}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.1
nodes.statement: Compose the four reductions: Lemma 5.5 (automorphisms), Lemma 5.9 (search/decision), Lemma 5.12 (worst/average), Lemma 5.14 (hybrid), using Lemma 5.13 to verify the hybrid premise.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5.2
nodes.statement: Same chain of reductions as in Theorem 5.1 but replace Lemma 5.12 with Lemma 5.16 (spherical-noise variant), yielding a fixed spherical noise $D_\xi$ at the cost of bounded samples $\ell$.

nodes.name: Cyclotomic embedding has unit roots
nodes.statement: For the $m$th cyclotomic field with $\zeta = \zeta_m$, embeddings $\sigma_i(\zeta) = \zeta^i$ for $i \in \mathbb{Z}_m^*$ are roots of unity, so $\|\zeta^j\|_2 = \sqrt{n}$ and $\|\zeta^j\|_\infty = 1$.

nodes.name: Trace and norm in $\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_5)$
nodes.statement: For $\zeta = \zeta_5$ with $\Phi_5(x) = x^4+x^3+x^2+x+1$ and $y = 1/2 - \zeta$: $\mathrm{Tr}(y) = 3$ and $N(y) = \Phi_5(1/2) = 31/16$.

nodes.name: Power basis is integral basis for cyclotomics
nodes.statement: For the $m$th cyclotomic $K = \mathbb{Q}(\zeta_m)$ of degree $n = \varphi(m)$, the power basis $\{1, \zeta_m, \dots, \zeta_m^{n-1}\}$ is also an integral basis: $\mathcal{O}_K = \mathbb{Z}[\zeta_m]$.

nodes.name: Splitting permits efficient ring operations
nodes.statement: When $q \equiv 1 \bmod m$, $\langle q\rangle$ splits completely into $n$ prime ideals of norm $q$; this complete splitting also enables fast ring operations (cf. companion paper [LPR13]).

nodes.name: Why work with $R^\vee$ rather than $R$
nodes.statement: Choosing $a \in R_q$ and $s \in R_q^\vee$ is mathematically natural and computationally optimal: for cyclotomics the codifferent $R^\vee$ minimizes $\lambda_n$ relative to ideal norm, so it admits the most spherical Gaussian decoding.

nodes.name: Ring-LWE (search)
nodes.statement: Distinguish/recover the secret $s \in R_q^\vee$ from polynomially many noisy ring samples $(a, b \approx a\cdot s/q + e)$, given an error distribution concentrated on small elements.

nodes.name: Approximate SVP / SIVP on ideal lattices
nodes.statement: Given a fractional ideal $I$ in a number field $K$, find a nonzero $x \in I$ with $\|x\| \leq \gamma \lambda_1(I)$ (SVP), or $n$ linearly independent vectors of norm $\leq \gamma \lambda_n(I)$ (SIVP).

nodes.name: Pick clearing element $t$
nodes.statement: Compute $t \in I$ such that $t \cdot I^{-1}$ is coprime to $\langle q \rangle$ via Lemma 2.14, using the factorization of $\langle q\rangle$.

nodes.name: Build LWE samples from Gaussian samples
nodes.statement: For each LWE oracle query, draw $z \sim D_{I,r}$ and small noise $e' \sim D_{\alpha/\sqrt{2}}$; output $a = \theta_t^{-1}(z \bmod qI) \in R_q$ and $b = (z\cdot y)/q + e' \bmod R^\vee$.

nodes.name: Recover BDD solution from LWE secret
nodes.statement: When the LWE oracle returns $s \in R_q^\vee$, output $\theta_t^{-1}(s) \in I_q^\vee$, which equals $x \bmod qI^\vee$.

nodes.name: Reduction 1: LWE → $\mathfrak{q}_i$-LWE
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5.5 (and the closure Lemma 5.6 for $\Psi_{\leq \alpha}$) to reduce $R$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ to $\mathfrak{q}_i$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ for any $i$.

nodes.name: Reduction 2: search to worst-case decision
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5.9 to reduce $\mathfrak{q}_i$-$\mathrm{LWE}_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ to $\mathrm{WDLWE}^i_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$.

nodes.name: Reduction 3: worst-case to average-case
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5.12 to reduce $\mathrm{WDLWE}^i_{q,\Psi_{\leq \alpha}}$ to $\mathrm{DLWE}^i_{q,\Upsilon_\alpha}$.

nodes.name: Reduction 4: hybrid argument
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma 5.14 (using Lemma 5.13 to verify the last-hybrid uniformity) to derive an algorithm for $\mathrm{DLWE}^i_{q,\Upsilon_\alpha}$ from any $\mathrm{DLWE}_{q,\Upsilon_\alpha}$ oracle.
